title: 3 Emerson AMS Condition Monitoring Alternatives
summary: Compare Tractian, SKF and Fluke Reliability as Emerson AMS alternatives on sensors, network needs, alert review, hazardous areas and CMMS integration.
body_markdown:
## Key Points


- Emerson AMS brings route, online and wireless data together in AMS Machine Works software.
- The biggest difference between alternatives is who diagnoses each alert before it reaches the planner.
- Tractian sensors send data to a receiver, and the receiver passes it on over 4G/LTE, so new coverage does not need a plant network project.


Of the three Emerson AMS alternatives worth comparing for condition monitoring, Tractian comes out on top, ahead of SKF and Fluke Reliability. Each one replaces or extends a different part of an AMS program: the handheld route, the online system or the wireless sensor layer.


This guide covers how Emerson AMS collects machinery data, why reliability teams review other options, and how the three alternatives compare on sensors, analysis, connectivity, hazardous areas and pricing. Plants comparing a wider field can weigh them against other[condition monitoring systems for heavy industry](https://tractian.com/en/blog/best-condition-monitoring-systems-heavy-industry) .


## What Is Emerson AMS for Condition Monitoring?


Emerson AMS is Emerson's family of machinery health products for rotating equipment such as pumps, motors, fans, compressors and turbines. It combines portable data collectors, wireless vibration sensors, online monitoring and protection systems, and AMS Machine Works software.


### How the AMS portfolio collects machinery data


AMS Machine Works is the software layer. It pulls measurements from the handheld, wireless, online and protection products below into one view of asset health.


- Handheld routes: the AMS 2140 Machinery Health Analyzer collects route data and handles vibration analysis, balancing and motor diagnostics in one unit.
- **Wireless sensors:** each AMS Wireless Vibration Monitor measures triax vibration, temperature and speed and sends readings over a WirelessHART network.
- **Online monitoring:** AMS Asset Monitor collects vibration and process data from balance-of-plant machines and runs embedded analytics for common faults, over wired or wireless Ethernet.
- **Protection:** the AMS 6500 ATG is a machinery protection and prediction system for critical assets such as compressors and turbines.


Emerson also sells AMS Machine Works Connect, a hosted bundle of sensor, gateway, router, SIM card, enclosure, software, cloud services, installation and configuration. Under that service, Emerson analysts hold weekly alarm reviews, and diagnostic reports arrive 24 to 72 hours after a finding.


### Emerson AMS pricing


Emerson sends AMS buyers to a customized quote request instead of a public price list.


## Why Do Teams Look at Emerson AMS Alternatives?


Teams often start looking when they want to extend coverage past the machines their AMS program already watches. Route data from a handheld analyzer arrives once per round, and a pump whose bearing starts to fail two days after the technician passes waits until the next visit. Learn more about[continuous vs periodic condition monitoring](https://tractian.com/en/blog/continuous-vs-periodic-condition-monitoring) .


Network and staffing questions come next. Wireless monitors report through WirelessHART gateways and online systems ride on plant Ethernet, so adding coverage in a new area can mean a network project as well as a sensor order. Staffing is the other factor: a plant that keeps diagnosis in-house needs people to review Machine Works data, and handing it to Emerson means adding the Machine Works Connect service.


Teams also compare vendors when each expansion needs its own quote, when they want AI that names the fault and the fix, or when alerts need to reach a CMMS outside the automation stack.

## Tractian


Best for: Plants that want wireless sensors and AI fault diagnosis on rotating assets that sit outside the reach of their current plant network.


Tractian is built around condition monitoring and AI-driven asset health: a sensor on the machine, models that interpret its signals, and an alert that names the fault, its severity and the fix. Tractian sensors talk to a receiver that carries the data on over 4G/LTE, with no plant Wi-Fi or new cable runs, so coverage can start in a tank farm or a cooling tower as easily as next to the control room.


### Notable features


One[Smart Trac Ultra](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/ultrasonic-sensor) mounts on each monitored machine and captures its vibration, ultrasound, temperature and RPM, with vibration sampled at up to 64 kHz on that asset. Its continuous ultrasound picks up friction from a starved bearing, and the technician can listen to the bearing while lubricating to apply the right amount.


[Auto Diagnosis](https://tractian.com/en/resources/videos/auto-diagnosis) links each signal pattern to a named failure mode, for example a worn bearing, a misaligned coupling or an unbalanced impeller. Severity and asset criticality decide where an alert lands in the queue, the alert lists probable root cause and next steps.


- **Electrical data:**[Energy Trac](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/energy-trac) sits in the panel supplying the motor, where it logs current, voltage and power factor. Its fault coverage includes rotor, stator, winding and insulation problems plus voltage imbalance.
- **Mechanical plus electrical:** together, Smart Trac Ultra on the asset and Energy Trac on its circuit form[multimodal monitoring](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/multimodal) , and Janus, Tractian's industrial AI, correlates the two signal sets with operating context to give one unified view of asset health.
- **Classified and washdown areas:** the IP69K sensors are[Class I Div 1 ATEX/IECEx/NFPA compliant](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/sensor-specifications) , and each one runs on its battery for up to 5 years.


### Implementation, reporting and integrations


- **Implementation:** adhesive or drill-and-tap mounting gets each sensor reporting in minutes. A deployment typically takes a day, needs no cable runs or plant Wi-Fi, and the models build a baseline on each pump or fan, with full visibility inside the first 14 days.
- **Reporting:** Power BI and SQL connectors feed custom reports, and a Looker connector supports customizable reports on failures and asset reliability.
- **Integrations:** alerts and asset records flow out through Tractian[integrations](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/integrations) to MaintainX, Fiix, UpKeep or Limble on the CMMS side and to SAP or Oracle NetSuite on the ERP side. Most SCADA and APM systems connect through the API.


### Customer results by industry


- [Food ingredients](https://tractian.com/en/industry/food-and-beverage) **:** before Tractian, a critical pump at[Ingredion](https://tractian.com/en/case-studies/ingredion) 's North Kansas City plant failed with no spare parts on hand and forced a three-day shutdown. With vibration sensors and AI diagnostics in place, one facility reports $1.0M in production savings, $223K in maintenance savings and 48 to 168 hours of downtime avoided on its critical machines.
- [Manufacturing](https://tractian.com/en/industry/manufacturing-maintenance-software) **:** a[Bosch](https://tractian.com/en/case-studies/bosch) facility with over 2,000 assets linked real-time vibration and temperature data from Tractian sensors to its own AI tool for repeat failures. The site cut recurring failures by 29% and raised planned maintenance by 17%.


### How much does Tractian cost to add next to AMS?


A Tractian quote starts from the machines on your list, not from a per-sensor catalog.[Tractian pricing](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/pricing) is per monitored asset. Share the pumps, fans and gearboxes you want protected and a specialist prepares the quote.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- Will Auto Diagnosis name the failure mode, severity and next step on our pumps and fans?
- Can a single sensor on each machine report vibration, ultrasound, temperature and RPM?
- How many days pass between mounting the first sensor and full diagnostics on our assets?
- Are the sensors Class I Div 1 ATEX/IECEx/NFPA compliant for the areas around our solvent and fuel handling?


## SKF


**Best for:** Plants that want SKF portable analyzers, wired online systems and wireless sensors analyzed in SKF software.


SKF's condition monitoring portfolio spans wired online systems, machine protection, wireless systems and portable devices, with analytical software and AI-based tools on top. Learn more about[SKF alternatives](https://tractian.com/en/blog/skf-alternatives) .


### Notable features


The SKF Enlight Collect IMx-1 wireless sensor reads overall and dynamic vibration, broadband acceleration and velocity, and temperature, and the IMx-1-EX version carries ATEX and IECEx approval for Zone 1.


Data from those devices goes to SKF @ptitude Observer, which detects issues through machine learning or an alarm and event log. Diagnosis runs through automated or rule-based AI, or by hand with vibration analysis plots, and results can be shared with historians, maintenance management systems and dashboards.


### SKF pricing


SKF sends buyers to its local distributors for sales and quotes.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- What has to be in place on site before IMx-1 sensors start sending data?
- Who supports installation and analysis when the system is bought through a distributor?
- Which maintenance systems receive @ptitude Observer results without custom work?


## Fluke Reliability


Best for: Plants that want Azima sensors, remote analysts and the eMaint CMMS from Fluke.


Fluke Reliability sells Azima wireless vibration sensors with WATCHMAN analytics, remote analyst services, portable vibration and laser alignment tools, and eMaint, the CMMS from Fluke. Learn more about[Fluke alternatives](https://tractian.com/en/blog/fluke-alternatives) .


### Notable features


Azima Accel 310 sensors measure triaxial vibration, carry a 3-year battery life and are IP and EX rated. WATCHMAN software turns the data into a fault diagnosis and a repair recommendation, and it issues hourly summaries plus a daily diagnostic analysis.


Fluke analysts can review WATCHMAN findings and run vibration analysis on request.


### Fluke Reliability pricing


Fluke Reliability shares sensor pricing through a conversation with a specialist, with no list price posted.


### Questions to ask before you buy


- [Who on our team would build eMaint reports and dashboards, and does that take a specialized skill set?](https://www.g2.com/products/emaint/reviews/emaint-review-13022568)
- Do the Accel 310 sensors read ultrasound or electrical data, or vibration alone?
- Which faults does WATCHMAN diagnose by itself, and when does a Fluke analyst step in?
- What does battery replacement involve once the 3-year life runs out?


## How Do You Choose an Emerson AMS Alternative?


Begin with the biggest gap in your current AMS program, whether route frequency, network reach, analyst time or hazardous-area coverage, and Tractian is built to close it from one platform.


Plant situation What to look for How Tractian fits


An AMS route program with vibration analysts on staff Continuous readings on the machines that drift between rounds, so analysts spend route time on troubleshooting Sensors stream data on the assets you pick, so analysts start from a named fault instead of a raw spectrum


WirelessHART gateways already tied to the control system Whether new coverage joins that network or runs on its own, and who maintains each path Sensors report over cellular, so the existing gateway network and its device count stay as they are


Hundreds of unmonitored balance-of-plant motors, pumps and fans Install effort per asset, cost per monitored point, and alerts that say what to fix Battery-powered sensors stick or stud-mount to each machine and send alerts ranked by severity


Classified areas around solvent, fuel or gas handling A certificate for the exact zone or division on your area classification drawing Sensors are Class I Div 1 ATEX/IECEx/NFPA compliant, with an IP69K housing for washdown


Remote units with no network drop, such as tank farms or cooling towers Connectivity that works where plant Wi-Fi and Ethernet do not reach 4G/LTE transmission sends data from the asset without a cable run back to the plant network


Before a plant-wide decision, put two or three vendors on the same short list of machines with a known fault history, such as a cooling water pump with repeat bearing changes or an induced draft fan with unbalance. Track which system flags the fault first, what the alert tells the planner, and how many minutes pass before the work order shows up in your CMMS. Plants with large unconnected areas can also compare options for[condition monitoring without a plant network](https://tractian.com/en/blog/condition-monitoring-without-plant-network) .


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is Emerson AMS used for?


Emerson AMS is the brand for Emerson's asset management products. For rotating machinery, it covers the AMS 2140 handheld analyzer, the AMS Wireless Vibration Monitor, AMS Asset Monitor, the AMS 6500 ATG protection system and AMS Machine Works software, which pulls their data into one view.


### Does Emerson AMS need wired sensors?


Part of the portfolio does. The AMS 2140 collects data on walking routes, and the AMS Wireless Vibration Monitor reports over a WirelessHART network. Online systems such as AMS Asset Monitor connect over wired or wireless Ethernet.


### How much does Emerson AMS cost?


Emerson quotes AMS projects on request rather than listing prices.


### What should you check before switching from Emerson AMS?


List the assets you monitor today and how each one is covered: route, online system or wireless sensor. Confirm that years of trend history can be exported, check what the new system needs from your network and IT team, and test how alerts reach your CMMS. A pilot on a handful of pumps and fans with known faults shows the difference faster than a feature list.


### Can wireless condition monitoring sensors run in classified areas?


Yes, when the sensor carries an approval for the zone or division where it will be mounted. Match the certificate to your area classification drawing before installation, including any gateway or receiver in the same area. For classified areas, Tractian sensors are Class I Div 1 ATEX/IECEx/NFPA compliant.
